cohort: 68 women with non-vertex singleton pregnancies (≥37 weeks) who had a failed ECV attempt without spinal anesthesia
finding: Repeat ECV with spinal anesthesia after a failed first attempt without spinal anesthesia increased the likelihood of vertex presentation at birth and decreased the cesarean delivery rate.
mod_finding: This study found that repeat external cephalic version with spinal anesthesia after a failed first attempt without spinal anesthesia decreased the rate of cesarean delivery.
